title: Join the pool
intro: Share this computer with the pool. While this tab is open, it runs an AI model on the graphics chip and does AI work for everyone in the pool.
share-note: You see each piece of work here. Close the tab to stop.
model-small: Small model, Qwen2.5 1.5B. An 870 MB download, about 1.6 GB of graphics memory. Runs on most computers.
model-strong: Strong model, Qwen3 4B. Better answers, also in Estonian. A 2.3 GB download, about 3.4 GB of graphics memory. Needs Apple Silicon with 16 GB or more, or a GeForce card with 6 GB or more.
model-largest: Largest model, Qwen3.5 9B. The best answers, also in Estonian, but slower. A 5 GB download, about 6.4 GB of graphics memory. Needs Apple Silicon with 16 GB or more, or a GeForce card with 8 GB or more.
does-run: Your browser downloads the model you chose (once) and runs it on your computer’s graphics chip with WebLLM. One model at a time: switching unloads the other.
does-answer: While you are in the pool, anyone who asks for that model (pool/qwen2.5-1.5b, pool/qwen3-4b or pool/qwen3.5-9b) gets the answer written here, and the words go back to them as they are written.
does-list: Each piece of work shows in the list above while it runs: the model, how many tokens, how many seconds.
does-usage: Each piece of work is also recorded on the usage page: the model, tokens, time, and your id as the one who served it, at no cost. Never what was asked or answered.
does-one: One at a time. If you stop or close the tab in the middle of one, a paid service finishes it.
never-files: It never opens your files, runs programs, or installs anything. A piece of work is only “write text for this prompt”.
never-keep: It doesn’t show or keep the prompts. They pass through this tab’s memory to the model and are gone.
never-who: It doesn’t tell you who asked. The usage page shows who served each piece of work, by id.
never-learn: The model doesn’t learn from prompts. It is a fixed file.
never-background: Nothing runs once this tab is closed: no background service.
never-incoming: Your computer accepts no incoming connections. This tab only connects out, to the addresses below.
addr-pool-why: this page, sign-in, and one outgoing connection for the work
addresses-note: The browser blocks every other address for this page (its Content Security Policy).
stores-title: What it stores, and how to stop
stores-what: The model files, in this browser’s storage for pool.visualia.space, and a sign-in cookie. Nothing else.
stores-stop: To stop: press Leave the pool, or close the tab.
stores-block: Whoever runs the pool can revoke your key, and IT can block pool.visualia.space.
code: The code is in the Visualia repository, apps/pool.
no-webgpu: This browser can’t join: it needs WebGPU. Use Chrome or Edge.
hint-strong: Graphics: {chip}. This looks strong enough for the bigger models, if the computer has the memory above.
hint-weak: Graphics: {chip}. The small model is the safe choice here.
welcome: In the pool with pool/{model}. Waiting for work. {n} computers in the pool, this one included.
welcome-alone: In the pool with pool/{model}. Waiting for work. This is the only computer in the pool right now.
connection-lost: Connection lost. Trying again in {seconds} s.
waiting: In the pool. Waiting for work.
removed: The models are removed from this browser.
